name: publicWeb_confirmAuthentication
description: The public web's half of the QR sign-in (E9.F7.S7). The page shows https://www.hashruns.org/login/UWP:<authCode>; the phone's app calls hcapp_authenticateWebPortal, which writes the HC.WebPortalAuthenticationRequests row. The Next.js server polls this SP until that row exists, then the browser is provisioned as an HC.Device (IsMobile = 0) bound to the hasher who scanned and the credentials are returned for the member cookie. Single-use (the request row is marked Removed) with a 5-minute TTL on WebPortalAuthenticationRequests.updatedAt — hcportal_confirmAuthentication minus the portal's service-account auth. No SP-level auth: the scanData match is the proof (a random value the page chose that only a signed-in phone can have recorded), and the SP is reachable only through PublicWebAdminApi behind HC_INTERNAL_SECRET, with @newDeviceId and @qrCodeData taken from a server-signed ticket.

parameters.name: newDeviceId
parameters.description: Device id the browser will use (from the server-signed ticket). NULL → no rows.

parameters.name: qrCodeData
parameters.description: The scan data as the app recorded it (compared case- and space-insensitively with WebPortalAuthenticationRequests.scanData). NULL or shorter than 10 characters → no rows.

parameters.name: deviceInfo
parameters.description: JSON with browserName / userAgent; stored as Device.DeviceData ('' when NULL) on a new device row.

rowsets.name: Credentials
rowsets.description: No rows while unscanned, expired, already consumed, the hasher Removed, or a parameter missing (the caller keeps polling). One row once a live request matches.

columns.name: deviceSecret
columns.description: The existing device's secret when @newDeviceId already has an HC.Device row, else a fresh 75-character secret (hcapp_authorizeDevice's recipe).

columns.name: timeWindow
columns.description: Token window in seconds (30-44 for a new device).

sideEffects: INSERT HC.Device (id = @newDeviceId, UserId, DeviceSecret, TimeWindow, DeviceData, IsMobile = 0) when no row exists for @newDeviceId — inside the transaction.
UPDATE HC.WebPortalAuthenticationRequests SET Removed = 1 for the matching scanData — single-use, same transaction.
INSERT HC.ErrorLog then THROW in the CATCH.

codeSmells.issue: Existing device row not checked against the hasher
codeSmells.detail: Lines 52-54 reuse the secret of any existing HC.Device row with id = @newDeviceId without checking its UserId or removed flag, and return it alongside the SCANNING hasher's identity. Harmless while @newDeviceId comes from a server-signed ticket with a fresh random id; it would hand out another device's secret if a caller could choose the id.

codeSmells.issue: Check-then-INSERT on HC.Device without a lock
codeSmells.detail: The existence read (line 53) is outside the transaction and unlocked; two concurrent polls with the same ticket would both INSERT the same id and one would fail with a PK violation (logged, re-thrown → 500). Polling is sequential today.

breakingChangeRules: Never remove a column from any rowset
Never change a sentinel value meaning
Never change errorType integer codes without updating all callers
